contains-duplicate.title: Contains Duplicate
contains-duplicate.markdown:
**Cue:** You only need to know whether a value has appeared before.

🔴 [MIT 6.006 — Hashing](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-4-hashing/) · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Hash Table](https://visualgo.net/en/hashtable)

**Return:** State the set invariant before each insertion and why the first failed insertion answers the question.

valid-anagram.title: Valid Anagram
valid-anagram.markdown:
**Cue:** Two strings are equivalent when every character has the same net frequency.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Hashing](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-4-hashing/) **(watch once; first at #1)** · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Hash Table](https://visualgo.net/en/hashtable)

**Return:** Define the frequency invariant and explain why length mismatch can be rejected immediately.

two-sum.title: Two Sum
two-sum.markdown:
**Cue:** For each value, ask whether its required complement has already appeared.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Hashing](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-4-hashing/) **(watch once; first at #1)** · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Hash Table](https://visualgo.net/en/hashtable)

**Return:** Explain why checking before inserting prevents pairing an element with itself and why one pass is enough.

group-anagrams.title: Group Anagrams
group-anagrams.markdown:
**Cue:** Design a canonical key so all strings in one equivalence class collide intentionally.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Hashing](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-4-hashing/) **(watch once; first at #1)** · 🔴 [MIT 6.006 — Sets and Sorting](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-3-sets-and-sorting/) · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Hash Table](https://visualgo.net/en/hashtable)

**Return:** Compare a sorted-string key with a frequency-vector key and include their costs in terms of word length.

top-k-frequent-elements.title: Top K Frequent Elements
top-k-frequent-elements.markdown:
**Cue:** Separate counting from selecting the largest frequencies.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Hashing](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-4-hashing/) **(watch once; first at #1)** · 🔴 [MIT 6.006 — Binary Heaps](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-8-binary-heaps/) · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Binary Heap](https://visualgo.net/en/heap)

**Return:** Explain the heap-size invariant or why bucket index equals frequency, then derive the full complexity.

product-of-array-except-self.title: Product of Array Except Self
product-of-array-except-self.markdown:
**Cue:** Precompute information from the left and right without division.

🔴 [USACO Guide — Prefix Sums](https://usaco.guide/silver/prefix-sums)

**Return:** Define what the output slot contains after the left pass and after the right pass; test zeros and length two.

valid-sudoku.title: Valid Sudoku
valid-sudoku.markdown:
**Cue:** Each filled cell participates in three independent uniqueness constraints.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Hashing](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-4-hashing/) **(watch once; first at #1)** · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Hash Table](https://visualgo.net/en/hashtable)

**Return:** Give the key used for row, column, and 3×3 box membership and show how the box index is calculated.

encode-and-decode-strings.title: Encode and Decode Strings
encode-and-decode-strings.markdown:
**Cue:** A stream needs unambiguous framing; raw delimiters are unsafe when payloads are unrestricted.

🔴 [Protocol Buffers — Encoding and Framing](https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/encoding/)

**Return:** Explain length-prefix framing, multi-digit lengths, empty strings, and the distinction between an empty list and one empty string.

longest-consecutive-sequence.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
longest-consecutive-sequence.markdown:
**Cue:** Only start walking from numbers that have no predecessor.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Hashing](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-4-hashing/) **(watch once; first at #1)** · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Hash Table](https://visualgo.net/en/hashtable)

**Return:** Prove that each run is counted once and that each value participates in only constant expected work.

valid-palindrome.title: Valid Palindrome
valid-palindrome.markdown:
**Cue:** Two indices can consume the only characters that still matter from opposite ends.

🔴 [USACO Guide — Two Pointers](https://usaco.guide/silver/two-pointers)

**Return:** State how each pointer skips irrelevant characters and why a mismatch cannot be repaired later.

two-sum-ii-input-array-is-sorted.title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
two-sum-ii-input-array-is-sorted.markdown:
**Cue:** Sorted order makes the sum move monotonically when either endpoint moves.

♻️ [USACO Guide — Two Pointers](https://usaco.guide/silver/two-pointers) **(watch once; first at #10)** · 🟡 [CP-Algorithms — Binary Search and Invariants](https://cp-algorithms.com/num_methods/binary_search.html)

**Return:** Prove which pointer must move when the sum is too small or too large.

3sum.title: 3Sum
3sum.markdown:
**Cue:** Sort once, fix one value, then solve a monotone two-sum search on the suffix.

♻️ [USACO Guide — Two Pointers](https://usaco.guide/silver/two-pointers) **(watch once; first at #10)** · ♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Sets and Sorting](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-3-sets-and-sorting/) **(watch once; first at #4)**

**Return:** Explain duplicate skipping at both the fixed index and moving pointers without skipping a distinct triplet.

container-with-most-water.title: Container With Most Water
container-with-most-water.markdown:
**Cue:** Area is limited by the shorter wall, so moving the taller wall cannot improve that pair.

♻️ [USACO Guide — Two Pointers](https://usaco.guide/silver/two-pointers) **(watch once; first at #10)**

**Return:** Give the dominance argument for discarding the shorter endpoint and include width in the invariant.

trapping-rain-water.title: Trapping Rain Water
trapping-rain-water.markdown:
**Cue:** Water at an index depends on the smaller of the best boundaries on both sides.

♻️ [USACO Guide — Two Pointers](https://usaco.guide/silver/two-pointers) **(watch once; first at #10)** · 🟡 [USACO Guide — Prefix Sums](https://usaco.guide/silver/prefix-sums)

**Return:** Explain why the side with the smaller current maximum can be finalized and test monotone and flat arrays.

best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.markdown:
**Cue:** Maintain the cheapest valid buy seen before the current sell.

🔴 [Sliding Window — Concept Walkthrough](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y2d0VHdvfdc) · 🟡 [USACO Guide — Sliding Window](https://usaco.guide/gold/sliding-window)

**Return:** State the meaning of the left boundary or running minimum and why a losing buy should be replaced.

longest-substring-without-repeating-char.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
longest-substring-without-repeating-char.markdown:
**Cue:** Maintain a window whose characters are unique.

♻️ [Sliding Window — Concept Walkthrough](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y2d0VHdvfdc) **(watch once; first at #15)** · 🟡 [USACO Guide — Sliding Window](https://usaco.guide/gold/sliding-window)

**Return:** Define window validity, visited timing, and why the left pointer never moves backward.

longest-repeating-character-replacement.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
longest-repeating-character-replacement.markdown:
**Cue:** A window is feasible when its non-majority characters fit within the replacement budget.

♻️ [Sliding Window — Concept Walkthrough](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y2d0VHdvfdc) **(watch once; first at #15)** · 🟡 [USACO Guide — Sliding Window](https://usaco.guide/gold/sliding-window)

**Return:** Derive `window length - maximum frequency <= k` and explain why a stale maximum frequency is still safe.

permutation-in-string.title: Permutation in String
permutation-in-string.markdown:
**Cue:** Every candidate has fixed length, so slide a frequency-difference window.

♻️ [Sliding Window — Concept Walkthrough](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y2d0VHdvfdc) **(watch once; first at #15)** · 🟡 [USACO Guide — Sliding Window](https://usaco.guide/gold/sliding-window)

**Return:** State what enters and leaves on every step and how validity is tested without recounting the whole window.

minimum-window-substring.title: Minimum Window Substring
minimum-window-substring.markdown:
**Cue:** Expand until all requirements are met, then shrink while validity remains.

♻️ [Sliding Window — Concept Walkthrough](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y2d0VHdvfdc) **(watch once; first at #15)** · 🟡 [USACO Guide — Sliding Window](https://usaco.guide/gold/sliding-window)

**Return:** Define the exact satisfied-requirements counter and prove that discarded left boundaries never need reconsideration.

sliding-window-maximum.title: Sliding Window Maximum
sliding-window-maximum.markdown:
**Cue:** Keep only nonexpired candidates that are not dominated by a newer, larger value.

🔴 [Labuladong — Monotonic Queue](https://labuladong.online/en/algo/data-structure/monotonic-queue/) · 🟡 [Monotonic Deque — Dry Runs](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cnOtN6T_zMY)

**Return:** State index order, value order, expiry, and why each index enters and leaves the deque at most once.

valid-parentheses.title: Valid Parentheses
valid-parentheses.markdown:
**Cue:** A closer must match the most recent unmatched opener.

🔴 [VisuAlgo — Stack, Queue, and Deque](https://visualgo.net/en/list)

**Return:** Define exactly what the stack represents after each character and handle an early closer and leftover openers.

min-stack.title: Min Stack
min-stack.markdown:
**Cue:** Augment every stack state with enough information to answer the minimum query immediately.

🔴 [CP-Algorithms — Minimum Stack and Queue](https://cp-algorithms.com/data_structures/stack_queue_modification.html) · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Stack, Queue, and Deque](https://visualgo.net/en/list)

**Return:** Explain the stored pair or second-stack invariant, especially when the minimum value appears more than once.

evaluate-reverse-polish-notation.title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
evaluate-reverse-polish-notation.markdown:
**Cue:** Postfix order makes every operator consume the two most recent complete operands.

🔴 [Reverse Polish Notation — Mental Model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reverse_Polish_notation) · ♻️ [VisuAlgo — Stack, Queue, and Deque](https://visualgo.net/en/list) **(watch once; first at #21)**

**Return:** State operand order for subtraction and division and why one final stack value remains.

daily-temperatures.title: Daily Temperatures
daily-temperatures.markdown:
**Cue:** Unresolved indices form a monotone stack until a warmer value resolves them.

🔴 [Labuladong — Monotonic Stack](https://labuladong.online/en/algo/data-structure/monotonic-stack/)

**Return:** State the stack’s value order, why indices are stored, and why each index is pushed and popped once.

car-fleet.title: Car Fleet
car-fleet.markdown:
**Cue:** After sorting by position, arrival times merge into a monotone sequence of fleets.

♻️ [Labuladong — Monotonic Stack](https://labuladong.online/en/algo/data-structure/monotonic-stack/) **(watch once; first at #24)** · 🔴 [CodePath — Greedy Algorithms](https://guides.codepath.org/compsci/Greedy-Algorithms) · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Sets and Sorting](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-3-sets-and-sorting/)

**Return:** Explain why a faster car behind cannot pass and when its arrival time is absorbed into the fleet ahead.

largest-rectangle-in-histogram.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
largest-rectangle-in-histogram.markdown:
**Cue:** An increasing stack delays a bar until its first smaller boundary is known.

♻️ [Labuladong — Monotonic Stack](https://labuladong.online/en/algo/data-structure/monotonic-stack/) **(watch once; first at #24)**

**Return:** For every popped bar, identify its height, exclusive right boundary, carried left boundary, and width.

binary-search.title: Binary Search
binary-search.markdown:
**Cue:** Maintain an interval guaranteed to contain every still-possible answer.

🔴 [CP-Algorithms — Binary Search and Invariants](https://cp-algorithms.com/num_methods/binary_search.html) · 🟡 [USACO Guide — Binary Search](https://usaco.guide/silver/binary-search)

**Return:** Choose a closed or half-open invariant and make every update preserve it without off-by-one ambiguity.

search-a-2d-matrix.title: Search a 2D Matrix
search-a-2d-matrix.markdown:
**Cue:** The matrix’s row ordering creates one conceptual sorted array.

♻️ [CP-Algorithms — Binary Search and Invariants](https://cp-algorithms.com/num_methods/binary_search.html) **(watch once; first at #27)** · 🟡 [Row-Major and Column-Major Order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Row-_and_column-major_order)

**Return:** Map a flattened index back to row and column and define the searchable interval precisely.

koko-eating-bananas.title: Koko Eating Bananas
koko-eating-bananas.markdown:
**Cue:** Binary-search the smallest speed satisfying a monotone feasibility predicate.

♻️ [CP-Algorithms — Binary Search and Invariants](https://cp-algorithms.com/num_methods/binary_search.html) **(watch once; first at #27)** · 🟡 [USACO Guide — Binary Search](https://usaco.guide/silver/binary-search)

**Return:** Write the predicate, prove faster speeds stay feasible, and state whether the boundaries are feasible or infeasible.

find-minimum-in-rotated-sorted-array.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
find-minimum-in-rotated-sorted-array.markdown:
**Cue:** Compare the middle with the right boundary to identify the unsorted side containing the pivot.

♻️ [CP-Algorithms — Binary Search and Invariants](https://cp-algorithms.com/num_methods/binary_search.html) **(watch once; first at #27)**

**Return:** Explain why `mid > right` discards the left including `mid`, while the opposite case keeps `mid`.

search-in-rotated-sorted-array.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
search-in-rotated-sorted-array.markdown:
**Cue:** At least one half around the middle is normally sorted.

♻️ [CP-Algorithms — Binary Search and Invariants](https://cp-algorithms.com/num_methods/binary_search.html) **(watch once; first at #27)**

**Return:** Identify the sorted half, test whether the target lies inside its value range, and preserve the search invariant.

time-based-key-value-store.title: Time Based Key-Value Store
time-based-key-value-store.markdown:
**Cue:** Append-only timestamps permit predecessor search inside each key’s history.

♻️ [CP-Algorithms — Binary Search and Invariants](https://cp-algorithms.com/num_methods/binary_search.html) **(watch once; first at #27)** · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Hashing](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-4-hashing/)

**Return:** Define the answer as the greatest timestamp not exceeding the query and handle “no predecessor” cleanly.

median-of-two-sorted-arrays.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
median-of-two-sorted-arrays.markdown:
**Cue:** Binary-search a partition whose two cross-boundary inequalities are valid.

♻️ [CP-Algorithms — Binary Search and Invariants](https://cp-algorithms.com/num_methods/binary_search.html) **(watch once; first at #27)** · 🛟 [Median Partition — Rescue Explanation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q6IEA26hvXc) **(only after 45–60 min solo)**

**Return:** Search the shorter array, write both partition inequalities and sentinels, and derive odd versus even median handling.

reverse-linked-list.title: Reverse Linked List
reverse-linked-list.markdown:
**Cue:** Rewire one edge at a time while preserving the unprocessed suffix.

🔴 [Pointer Reversal — Linked List](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O0By4Zq0OFc) · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Linked List](https://visualgo.net/en/list)

**Return:** Before each assignment, name `previous`, `current`, and the saved next node; prove no nodes are lost.

merge-two-sorted-lists.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
merge-two-sorted-lists.markdown:
**Cue:** Advance the smaller frontier and attach it to a growing sorted prefix.

🔴 [VisuAlgo — Linked List](https://visualgo.net/en/list)

**Return:** Define what the tail points to and why attaching the remaining suffix is safe.

linked-list-cycle.title: Linked List Cycle
linked-list-cycle.markdown:
**Cue:** A linked list is a deterministic state transition, so repeated nodes form a cycle.

🔴 [CP-Algorithms — Tortoise and Hare](https://cp-algorithms.com/others/tortoise_and_hare.html) · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Linked List](https://visualgo.net/en/list)

**Return:** Explain why fast eventually meets slow in a cycle and why null terminates the acyclic case.

reorder-list.title: Reorder List
reorder-list.markdown:
**Cue:** Compose three primitives: find the midpoint, reverse the second half, then weave both halves.

♻️ [Pointer Reversal — Linked List](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O0By4Zq0OFc) **(watch once; first at #34)** · ♻️ [CP-Algorithms — Tortoise and Hare](https://cp-algorithms.com/others/tortoise_and_hare.html) **(watch once; first at #36)** · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Linked List](https://visualgo.net/en/list)

**Return:** State where the first half ends, how the second is reversed, and which next pointers must be saved while weaving.

remove-nth-node-from-end-of-list.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
remove-nth-node-from-end-of-list.markdown:
**Cue:** A fixed gap between two pointers converts an end-relative position into a forward scan.

♻️ [USACO Guide — Two Pointers](https://usaco.guide/silver/two-pointers) **(watch once; first at #10)** · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Linked List](https://visualgo.net/en/list)

**Return:** Define the gap, explain the dummy node, and show where the slow pointer stops before deletion.

copy-list-with-random-pointer.title: Copy List with Random Pointer
copy-list-with-random-pointer.markdown:
**Cue:** Clone identity separately from wiring so arbitrary references can be reconstructed.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Hashing](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-4-hashing/) **(watch once; first at #1)** · ♻️ [VisuAlgo — Linked List](https://visualgo.net/en/list) **(watch once; first at #35)**

**Return:** Explain the old-to-new mapping or interleaving invariant and why random pointers must target clones, not originals.

add-two-numbers.title: Add Two Numbers
add-two-numbers.markdown:
**Cue:** Simulate grade-school addition while digits arrive least significant first.

🔴 [Positional Notation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Positional_notation) · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Linked List](https://visualgo.net/en/list)

**Return:** State the carry invariant, how unequal lengths are handled, and when a final carry creates a node.

find-the-duplicate-number.title: Find the Duplicate Number
find-the-duplicate-number.markdown:
**Cue:** Treat each array value as a next pointer in a functional graph.

♻️ [CP-Algorithms — Tortoise and Hare](https://cp-algorithms.com/others/tortoise_and_hare.html) **(watch once; first at #36)**

**Return:** Explain why a cycle must exist and derive both Floyd phases, including why the second meeting is the duplicate.

lru-cache.title: LRU Cache
lru-cache.markdown:
**Cue:** Combine O(1) lookup with O(1) movement and eviction in recency order.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Hashing](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-4-hashing/) **(watch once; first at #1)** · ♻️ [VisuAlgo — Linked List](https://visualgo.net/en/list) **(watch once; first at #35)**

**Return:** Define head/tail sentinel roles, the map-to-node invariant, and every pointer update for remove and insert.

merge-k-sorted-lists.title: Merge k Sorted Lists
merge-k-sorted-lists.markdown:
**Cue:** Only the current head of each sorted stream can be the next global minimum.

🔴 [K-Way Merge with a Heap](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ptYUCjfNhJY) · ♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Binary Heaps](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-8-binary-heaps/) **(watch once; first at #5)** · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Binary Heap](https://visualgo.net/en/heap)

**Return:** Explain why one candidate per list is sufficient and how popping exposes exactly one replacement candidate.

reverse-nodes-in-k-group.title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
reverse-nodes-in-k-group.markdown:
**Cue:** Reverse a bounded segment while preserving both its prefix connection and untouched suffix.

♻️ [Pointer Reversal — Linked List](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O0By4Zq0OFc) **(watch once; first at #34)** · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Linked List](https://visualgo.net/en/list)

**Return:** Before rewiring, identify the group predecessor, kth node, saved suffix, and new group tail.

invert-binary-tree.title: Invert Binary Tree
invert-binary-tree.markdown:
**Cue:** A tree transformation is defined locally and applied recursively to both subtrees.

🔴 [MIT 6.006 — Binary Trees, Part 1](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-6-binary-trees-part-1/) · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Binary Search Tree](https://visualgo.net/en/bst)

**Return:** State the recursive contract and whether swapping occurs before or after recursive calls.

maximum-depth-of-binary-tree.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
maximum-depth-of-binary-tree.markdown:
**Cue:** A node’s answer is one plus the larger child answer.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Binary Trees, Part 1](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-6-binary-trees-part-1/) **(watch once; first at #45)** · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Recursion](https://visualgo.net/en/recursion)

**Return:** Define the empty-tree base case and what each recursive call returns.

diameter-of-binary-tree.title: Diameter of Binary Tree
diameter-of-binary-tree.markdown:
**Cue:** The returned one-arm height and the best path passing through a node are different quantities.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Binary Trees, Part 1](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-6-binary-trees-part-1/) **(watch once; first at #45)**

**Return:** Explain what recursion returns, what updates the global answer, and whether diameter counts nodes or edges.

balanced-binary-tree.title: Balanced Binary Tree
balanced-binary-tree.markdown:
**Cue:** Return height together with failure information so no subtree is recomputed.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Binary Trees, Part 1](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-6-binary-trees-part-1/) **(watch once; first at #45)**

**Return:** Define the sentinel or pair contract and the exact condition that propagates imbalance upward.

same-tree.title: Same Tree
same-tree.markdown:
**Cue:** Compare two recursive structures in lockstep.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Binary Trees, Part 1](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-6-binary-trees-part-1/) **(watch once; first at #45)**

**Return:** List the both-null, one-null, unequal-value, and recursive cases in a complete order.

subtree-of-another-tree.title: Subtree of Another Tree
subtree-of-another-tree.markdown:
**Cue:** At each candidate root, separate “same tree here” from “search below.”

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Binary Trees, Part 1](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-6-binary-trees-part-1/) **(watch once; first at #45)**

**Return:** Explain the two recursive predicates and the empty-subtree convention.

lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-searc.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-searc.markdown:
**Cue:** BST ordering tells whether both targets lie on one side or split at the current node.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Binary Trees, Part 1](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-6-binary-trees-part-1/) **(watch once; first at #45)** · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Binary Search Tree](https://visualgo.net/en/bst)

**Return:** State all three ordering cases and why the first split point is the lowest common ancestor.

binary-tree-level-order-traversal.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
binary-tree-level-order-traversal.markdown:
**Cue:** A queue frontier represents exactly one BFS layer at a time.

🔴 [MIT 6.006 — Breadth-First Search](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-9-breadth-first-search/) · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — DFS and BFS](https://visualgo.net/en/dfsbfs)

**Return:** Capture the level size before processing and explain why newly enqueued children belong to the next level.

binary-tree-right-side-view.title: Binary Tree Right Side View
binary-tree-right-side-view.markdown:
**Cue:** The visible node is the last or first node encountered at each depth, depending on traversal order.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Breadth-First Search](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-9-breadth-first-search/) **(watch once; first at #52)** · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — DFS and BFS](https://visualgo.net/en/dfsbfs)

**Return:** Choose BFS or right-first DFS and state the invariant that selects exactly one node per depth.

count-good-nodes-in-binary-tree.title: Count Good Nodes in Binary Tree
count-good-nodes-in-binary-tree.markdown:
**Cue:** Carry the maximum value on the current root-to-node path.

🔴 [MIT 6.006 — Depth-First Search](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-10-depth-first-search/) · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Binary Trees, Part 1](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-6-binary-trees-part-1/)

construct-binary-tree-from-preorder-and-.title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
construct-binary-tree-from-preorder-and-.markdown:

**Return:** Define recursive index ranges, use a value-to-inorder-index map, and avoid slicing costs.

binary-tree-maximum-path-sum.title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
binary-tree-maximum-path-sum.markdown:
**Cue:** A parent can extend only one child branch, while the global answer may use both.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Binary Trees, Part 1](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-6-binary-trees-part-1/) **(watch once; first at #45)** · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Dynamic Programming I](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-15-dynamic-programming-part-1-srtbot-fib-dags-bowling/)

serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree.title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree.markdown:
**Cue:** Serialization needs traversal order plus explicit structure markers.

♻️ [Protocol Buffers — Encoding and Framing](https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/encoding/) **(watch once; first at #8)** · ♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Binary Trees, Part 1](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-6-binary-trees-part-1/) **(watch once; first at #45)**

kth-largest-element-in-a-stream.title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
kth-largest-element-in-a-stream.markdown:
**Cue:** A min-heap of size k keeps exactly the k largest values seen so far.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Binary Heaps](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-8-binary-heaps/) **(watch once; first at #5)** · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Binary Heap](https://visualgo.net/en/heap)

last-stone-weight.title: Last Stone Weight
last-stone-weight.markdown:
**Cue:** Repeatedly extract the two largest elements, so the data structure must expose maxima efficiently.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Binary Heaps](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-8-binary-heaps/) **(watch once; first at #5)** · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Binary Heap](https://visualgo.net/en/heap)

**Return:** Trace one collision and derive the number of heap operations and total complexity.

k-closest-points-to-origin.title: K Closest Points to Origin
k-closest-points-to-origin.markdown:
**Cue:** Selection needs only a comparable key; square roots are unnecessary.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Binary Heaps](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-8-binary-heaps/) **(watch once; first at #5)** · 🟡 [Princeton Algorithms — Quicksort and Selection](https://algs4.cs.princeton.edu/23quicksort/)

kth-largest-element-in-an-array.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
kth-largest-element-in-an-array.markdown:
**Cue:** Partition-based selection discards the side that cannot contain the target rank.

🔴 [Princeton Algorithms — Quicksort and Selection](https://algs4.cs.princeton.edu/23quicksort/) · 🟡 [MIT 6.046 — Randomized Median](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-046j-design-and-analysis-of-algorithms-spring-2015/resources/recitation-4-randomization-randomized-median/) · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Binary Heaps](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-8-binary-heaps/)

**Return:** Translate kth largest into a zero-based sorted index and state the partition invariant.

task-scheduler.title: Task Scheduler
task-scheduler.markdown:
**Cue:** The most frequent tasks determine idle pressure; a heap can simulate available choices over cooldown time.

♻️ [CodePath — Greedy Algorithms](https://guides.codepath.org/compsci/Greedy-Algorithms) **(watch once; first at #25)** · ♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Binary Heaps](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-8-binary-heaps/) **(watch once; first at #5)**

**Return:** Explain the frequency lower bound or the heap-plus-cooldown invariant and test a case with no required idles.

design-twitter.title: Design Twitter
design-twitter.markdown:
**Cue:** Merge the newest frontier from several timestamp-sorted streams.

♻️ [K-Way Merge with a Heap](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ptYUCjfNhJY) **(watch once; first at #43)** · 🟡 [ByteByteGo — News Feed Design](https://bytebytego.com/courses/system-design-interview/design-a-news-feed-system) · 🟡 [System Design Primer — Twitter](https://github.com/donnemartin/system-design-primer/blob/master/solutions/system_design/twitter/README.md)

find-median-from-data-stream.title: Find Median from Data Stream
find-median-from-data-stream.markdown:
**Cue:** Maintain lower and upper halves whose boundary values expose the median.

🔴 [Two Heaps for a Running Median](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VmogG01IjYc) · ♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Binary Heaps](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-8-binary-heaps/) **(watch once; first at #5)** · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Binary Heap](https://visualgo.net/en/heap)

**Return:** State the allowed size difference and ordering relation between the max-heap and min-heap.

subsets.title: Subsets
subsets.markdown:
**Cue:** At each position, choose whether the element belongs to the current subset.

🔴 [Stanford CS106B — Backtracking](https://web.stanford.edu/class/archive/cs/cs106b/cs106b.1258/lectures/11-backtracking1/) · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Recursion](https://visualgo.net/en/recursion)

**Return:** Define the decision-tree state, when output is recorded, and how the path is restored.

combination-sum.title: Combination Sum
combination-sum.markdown:
**Cue:** Build nondecreasing combinations so the same multiset is not generated in different orders.

♻️ [Stanford CS106B — Backtracking](https://web.stanford.edu/class/archive/cs/cs106b/cs106b.1258/lectures/11-backtracking1/) **(watch once; first at #67)** · 🟡 [Backtracking Template — Concept Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vqnZ9RhhkmY)

combination-sum-ii.title: Combination Sum II
combination-sum-ii.markdown:
**Cue:** Sort candidates and skip equal choices only when they compete at the same recursion depth.

**Return:** Explain same-depth duplicate skipping, why the next call advances the index, and when to stop the loop.

permutations.title: Permutations
permutations.markdown:
**Cue:** Every position chooses one still-unused element.

♻️ [Stanford CS106B — Backtracking](https://web.stanford.edu/class/archive/cs/cs106b/cs106b.1258/lectures/11-backtracking1/) **(watch once; first at #67)** · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Recursion](https://visualgo.net/en/recursion)

**Return:** Choose a used set or in-place swap invariant and show how each complete ordering appears exactly once.

subsets-ii.title: Subsets II
subsets-ii.markdown:
**Cue:** Sorting makes duplicate branches adjacent so equivalent choices can be suppressed per depth.

♻️ [Stanford CS106B — Backtracking](https://web.stanford.edu/class/archive/cs/cs106b/cs106b.1258/lectures/11-backtracking1/) **(watch once; first at #67)** · ♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Sets and Sorting](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-3-sets-and-sorting/) **(watch once; first at #4)**

**Return:** Explain why skipping duplicates across siblings is correct but skipping the value at deeper levels is not.

generate-parentheses.title: Generate Parentheses
generate-parentheses.markdown:
**Cue:** Generate only prefixes that can still be completed into a valid string.

♻️ [Stanford CS106B — Backtracking](https://web.stanford.edu/class/archive/cs/cs106b/cs106b.1258/lectures/11-backtracking1/) **(watch once; first at #67)** · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Recursion](https://visualgo.net/en/recursion)

**Return:** State the constraints `open <= n` and `close <= open`, plus the exact completion condition.

word-search.title: Word Search
word-search.markdown:
**Cue:** The board path is a backtracking state: choose a neighbor, mark it, explore, then restore.

♻️ [Stanford CS106B — Backtracking](https://web.stanford.edu/class/archive/cs/cs106b/cs106b.1258/lectures/11-backtracking1/) **(watch once; first at #67)** · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — DFS and BFS](https://visualgo.net/en/dfsbfs)

**Return:** Name the board mutation, restoration point, boundary checks, and why a cell cannot be reused in one path.

palindrome-partitioning.title: Palindrome Partitioning
palindrome-partitioning.markdown:
**Cue:** Each recursion chooses the next palindromic prefix and partitions the remaining suffix.

♻️ [Stanford CS106B — Backtracking](https://web.stanford.edu/class/archive/cs/cs106b/cs106b.1258/lectures/11-backtracking1/) **(watch once; first at #67)** · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Dynamic Programming II: Coins, LIS, LCS](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-16-dynamic-programming-part-2-lcs-lis-coins/)

letter-combinations-of-a-phone-number.title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number

**Return:** Derive the two diagonal keys, state all maintained sets, and show exactly where each choice is undone.

implement-trie-prefix-tree.title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
implement-trie-prefix-tree.markdown:

design-add-and-search-words-data-structu.title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure

word-search-ii.title: Word Search II

number-of-islands.title: Number of Islands

redundant-connection.title: Redundant Connection

🔴 [Union-Find — Concept Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ibjEGG7ylHk) · 🟡 [CP-Algorithms — Disjoint Set Union](https://cp-algorithms.com/data_structures/disjoint_set_union.html) · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Union-Find](https://visualgo.net/en/ufds)

min-cost-to-connect-all-points.markdown:

alien-dictionary.title: Alien Dictionary

climbing-stairs.markdown:
**Cue:** The number of ways to reach a step is the sum of ways to its legal predecessor steps.

🔴 [Dynamic Programming — Five-Step Framework](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aPQY__2H3tE) · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Dynamic Programming I](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-15-dynamic-programming-part-1-srtbot-fib-dags-bowling/)

**Return:** Define `dp[i]`, recurrence, base cases, and evaluation order before compressing space.

min-cost-climbing-stairs.title: Min Cost Climbing Stairs
min-cost-climbing-stairs.markdown:
**Cue:** The state should represent the minimum cost to arrive at a position, including the virtual top.

♻️ [Dynamic Programming — Five-Step Framework](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aPQY__2H3tE) **(watch once; first at #99)** · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Dynamic Programming I](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-15-dynamic-programming-part-1-srtbot-fib-dags-bowling/)

**Return:** Choose whether cost is paid on entering or leaving a step and make bases and recurrence consistent.

house-robber.title: House Robber
house-robber.markdown:
**Cue:** A choice blocks its neighbor, so summarize the best value for each prefix.

♻️ [Dynamic Programming — Five-Step Framework](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aPQY__2H3tE) **(watch once; first at #99)** · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Dynamic Programming I](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-15-dynamic-programming-part-1-srtbot-fib-dags-bowling/)

**Return:** Define the state in words, its two predecessors, recurrence, bases, and evaluation order.

house-robber-ii.title: House Robber II
house-robber-ii.markdown:
**Cue:** Circular adjacency becomes two linear cases that cannot both include the endpoints.

♻️ [Dynamic Programming — Five-Step Framework](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aPQY__2H3tE) **(watch once; first at #99)** · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Dynamic Programming I](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-15-dynamic-programming-part-1-srtbot-fib-dags-bowling/)

**Return:** Explain why excluding the first or excluding the last covers every valid solution, including tiny arrays.

longest-palindromic-substring.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
longest-palindromic-substring.markdown:
🚫 **No pre-watch.** A palindrome grows symmetrically around an odd or even center.

🟡 **After solve:** [CP-Algorithms — Manacher’s Algorithm](https://cp-algorithms.com/string/manacher.html)

**Return:** Derive center expansion first, count the `2n-1` centers, and compare its complexity with Manacher’s algorithm.

palindromic-substrings.title: Palindromic Substrings
palindromic-substrings.markdown:
🚫 **No pre-watch.** Every palindrome is identified by an odd or even center and maximal matching expansion.

🟡 **After solve:** [CP-Algorithms — Manacher’s Algorithm](https://cp-algorithms.com/string/manacher.html)

**Return:** Explain the `2n-1` centers and why each successful expansion corresponds to exactly one substring.

decode-ways.title: Decode Ways
decode-ways.markdown:
**Cue:** A prefix can end with one valid digit or one valid two-digit code.

♻️ [Dynamic Programming — Five-Step Framework](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aPQY__2H3tE) **(watch once; first at #99)** · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Dynamic Programming I](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-15-dynamic-programming-part-1-srtbot-fib-dags-bowling/)

**Return:** Define the prefix state, zero-handling rules, and both predecessor contributions.

coin-change.title: Coin Change
coin-change.markdown:
**Cue:** Amounts are states and each coin creates a transition from a smaller amount.

🔴 [MIT 6.006 — Dynamic Programming II: Coins, LIS, LCS](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-16-dynamic-programming-part-2-lcs-lis-coins/) · 🟡 [CP-Algorithms — 0/1 and Unbounded Knapsack](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/knapsack.html)

**Return:** Define `dp[a]`, its incoming transitions, and an unreachable sentinel that cannot look optimal.

maximum-product-subarray.title: Maximum Product Subarray
maximum-product-subarray.markdown:
**Cue:** A negative number can swap the useful maximum and minimum products ending here.

♻️ [Dynamic Programming — Five-Step Framework](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aPQY__2H3tE) **(watch once; first at #99)** · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Dynamic Programming I](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-15-dynamic-programming-part-1-srtbot-fib-dags-bowling/)

**Return:** Explain why both extremes must be carried and how zero resets the possibilities.

word-break.title: Word Break
word-break.markdown:
**Cue:** A prefix is reachable when a previous reachable prefix is followed by one dictionary word.

♻️ [Dynamic Programming — Five-Step Framework](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aPQY__2H3tE) **(watch once; first at #99)** · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Hashing](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-4-hashing/)

**Return:** Define the prefix state and transition, then include substring or trie costs in the complexity.

longest-increasing-subsequence.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
longest-increasing-subsequence.markdown:
**Cue:** Start with sequence DP; then interpret minimal tails for the faster method.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Dynamic Programming II: Coins, LIS, LCS](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-16-dynamic-programming-part-2-lcs-lis-coins/) **(watch once; first at #106)** · 🟡 [CP-Algorithms — Longest Increasing Subsequence](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/longest_increasing_subsequence.html) · 🟡 [Patience Sorting and LIS — Intuition](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=22s1xxRvy28)

**Return:** Derive the quadratic recurrence, then explain why `tails[length]` is a minimal tail rather than the final subsequence.

partition-equal-subset-sum.title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
partition-equal-subset-sum.markdown:
**Cue:** Equal partition is a 0/1 subset-sum feasibility problem at half the total.

🔴 [CP-Algorithms — 0/1 and Unbounded Knapsack](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/knapsack.html) · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Subset Sum and Pseudopolynomial DP](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-18-dynamic-programming-part-4-rods-subset-sum-pseudopolynomial/)

**Return:** Check parity, explain downward capacity iteration, and state why the runtime is pseudopolynomial.

unique-paths.title: Unique Paths
unique-paths.markdown:
**Cue:** Each grid state depends only on the cell above and the cell to the left.

♻️ [Dynamic Programming — Five-Step Framework](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aPQY__2H3tE) **(watch once; first at #99)** · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Dynamic Programming I](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-15-dynamic-programming-part-1-srtbot-fib-dags-bowling/)

**Return:** Define the state, predecessor transitions, and boundary initialization without scattered special cases.

longest-common-subsequence.title: Longest Common Subsequence
longest-common-subsequence.markdown:
**Cue:** Use two prefix lengths as the state for aligning two sequences.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Dynamic Programming II: Coins, LIS, LCS](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-16-dynamic-programming-part-2-lcs-lis-coins/) **(watch once; first at #106)** · 🟡 [MIT — Sequence Alignment Grid](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/7-91j-foundations-of-computational-and-systems-biology-spring-2014/resources/lecture-3-global-alignment-of-protein-sequences-nw-sw-pam-blosum/)

**Return:** Separate matching and nonmatching cases and show every transition shrinks at least one prefix.

best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock-with-coo.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Cooldown
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock-with-coo.markdown:
**Cue:** Model legal holding, sold, and resting statuses as a finite-state machine.

🔴 [State-Machine Dynamic Programming](https://www.thealgorists.com/Algo/DynamicProgramming/StateMachineConcept/Fundamentals) · 🟡 [Labuladong — Stock DP State Machine](https://labuladong.online/en/algo/dynamic-programming/stock-problem-summary/)

**Return:** Name each state, every legal transition, and the transition that enforces the cooldown.

coin-change-ii.title: Coin Change II
coin-change-ii.markdown:
**Cue:** Counting combinations makes loop order part of correctness.

♻️ [CP-Algorithms — 0/1 and Unbounded Knapsack](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/knapsack.html) **(watch once; first at #110)** · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Dynamic Programming II: Coins, LIS, LCS](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-16-dynamic-programming-part-2-lcs-lis-coins/)

**Return:** Explain why coin-first with increasing amounts counts each multiset once rather than counting permutations.

target-sum.title: Target Sum
target-sum.markdown:
**Cue:** Signed choices can be represented directly or reduced to a counting subset-sum problem.

♻️ [CP-Algorithms — 0/1 and Unbounded Knapsack](https://cp-algorithms.com/dynamic_programming/knapsack.html) **(watch once; first at #110)** · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Subset Sum and Pseudopolynomial DP](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-18-dynamic-programming-part-4-rods-subset-sum-pseudopolynomial/)

**Return:** Derive the reduction including parity and feasibility conditions, or define the signed-state offset.

interleaving-string.title: Interleaving String
interleaving-string.markdown:
**Cue:** Two source indices determine the consumed destination index.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Dynamic Programming II: Coins, LIS, LCS](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-16-dynamic-programming-part-2-lcs-lis-coins/) **(watch once; first at #106)** · 🟡 [MIT — Sequence Alignment Grid](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/7-91j-foundations-of-computational-and-systems-biology-spring-2014/resources/lecture-3-global-alignment-of-protein-sequences-nw-sw-pam-blosum/)

**Return:** Name the two legal predecessors into `(i, j)` and explain why the destination index is `i + j`.

longest-increasing-path-in-a-matrix.title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
longest-increasing-path-in-a-matrix.markdown:
**Cue:** Strictly increasing moves form a DAG, so memoized DFS solves each cell once.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Depth-First Search](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-10-depth-first-search/) **(watch once; first at #54)** · 🟡 [CP-Algorithms — Topological Sorting](https://cp-algorithms.com/graph/topological-sort.html)

**Return:** Explain acyclicity, the memoized state meaning, and why no visiting-state cycle handling is required.

distinct-subsequences.title: Distinct Subsequences
distinct-subsequences.markdown:
**Cue:** Count ways to form target prefixes from source prefixes by using or skipping source characters.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Dynamic Programming II: Coins, LIS, LCS](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-16-dynamic-programming-part-2-lcs-lis-coins/) **(watch once; first at #106)** · 🟡 [MIT — Sequence Alignment Grid](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/7-91j-foundations-of-computational-and-systems-biology-spring-2014/resources/lecture-3-global-alignment-of-protein-sequences-nw-sw-pam-blosum/)

**Return:** At a match, separate use and skip; with 1-D compression, justify backward target iteration.

edit-distance.title: Edit Distance
edit-distance.markdown:
**Cue:** Edit operations are neighboring transitions in a two-prefix alignment grid.

🔴 [MIT — Sequence Alignment Grid](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/7-91j-foundations-of-computational-and-systems-biology-spring-2014/resources/lecture-3-global-alignment-of-protein-sequences-nw-sw-pam-blosum/) · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Dynamic Programming II: Coins, LIS, LCS](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-16-dynamic-programming-part-2-lcs-lis-coins/)

**Return:** Map insertion, deletion, and substitution to cells and justify both empty-string borders.

burst-balloons.title: Burst Balloons
burst-balloons.markdown:
**Cue:** Choose the last action inside an interval so both outside boundaries are fixed.

🔴 [MIT 6.006 — Dynamic Programming III: Interval DP](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-17-dynamic-programming-part-3-apsp-parens-piano/) · 🟡 [Interval DP — Concept Tutorial](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5q9vCX0Y9Uo)

**Return:** Define the open interval, choose the last balloon, and show how the two independent subintervals combine.

regular-expression-matching.title: Regular Expression Matching
regular-expression-matching.markdown:
**Cue:** Treat `.` and `*` as transitions in a small pattern machine over two prefixes.

🔴 [Russ Cox — Regular Expressions as NFAs](https://swtch.com/~rsc/regexp/regexp1.html) · 🟡 [Princeton Algorithms — Regular Expressions](https://algs4.cs.princeton.edu/54regexp/)

**Return:** Define `dp[i][j]`; for `*`, derive zero copies versus consuming one matching character.

maximum-subarray.title: Maximum Subarray
maximum-subarray.markdown:
**Cue:** A negative running prefix can only hurt every future subarray that includes it.

♻️ [CodePath — Greedy Algorithms](https://guides.codepath.org/compsci/Greedy-Algorithms) **(watch once; first at #25)** · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Dynamic Programming I](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-15-dynamic-programming-part-1-srtbot-fib-dags-bowling/)

**Return:** Define the best sum ending here, the global best, and why resetting after a harmful prefix is safe.

jump-game.title: Jump Game
jump-game.markdown:
**Cue:** Maintain the farthest index reachable from the processed prefix.

♻️ [CodePath — Greedy Algorithms](https://guides.codepath.org/compsci/Greedy-Algorithms) **(watch once; first at #25)** · 🟡 [Greedy Invariants — Concept Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W1hdYdsqBJo)

**Return:** State the reachable-prefix invariant and the exact point at which progress becomes impossible.

jump-game-ii.title: Jump Game II
jump-game-ii.markdown:
**Cue:** Treat the current reachable interval like one BFS layer and build the next farthest boundary.

♻️ [CodePath — Greedy Algorithms](https://guides.codepath.org/compsci/Greedy-Algorithms) **(watch once; first at #25)** · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Breadth-First Search](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-9-breadth-first-search/)

**Return:** Define current layer end, farthest next reach, and when the jump count increments.

gas-station.title: Gas Station
gas-station.markdown:
**Cue:** A failed partial route proves every station inside that failed segment is also an invalid start.

♻️ [CodePath — Greedy Algorithms](https://guides.codepath.org/compsci/Greedy-Algorithms) **(watch once; first at #25)** · 🟡 [Greedy Invariants — Concept Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W1hdYdsqBJo)

**Return:** Separate total feasibility from candidate reset and give the proof for skipping failed starts.

hand-of-straights.title: Hand of Straights
hand-of-straights.markdown:
**Cue:** The smallest remaining card must begin a group, so greedily consume consecutive counts.

♻️ [CodePath — Greedy Algorithms](https://guides.codepath.org/compsci/Greedy-Algorithms) **(watch once; first at #25)** · ♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Hashing](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-4-hashing/) **(watch once; first at #1)** · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Binary Heaps](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-8-binary-heaps/)

**Return:** Explain why the minimum cannot be placed later and how zero counts are removed without breaking order.

merge-triplets-to-form-target-triplet.title: Merge Triplets to Form Target Triplet
merge-triplets-to-form-target-triplet.markdown:
**Cue:** Any triplet exceeding the target in one coordinate is permanently unusable.

♻️ [CodePath — Greedy Algorithms](https://guides.codepath.org/compsci/Greedy-Algorithms) **(watch once; first at #25)**

**Return:** After filtering overshoots, explain why independently witnessing each target coordinate is sufficient.

partition-labels.title: Partition Labels
partition-labels.markdown:
**Cue:** A segment must extend through the last occurrence of every character it already contains.

♻️ [CodePath — Greedy Algorithms](https://guides.codepath.org/compsci/Greedy-Algorithms) **(watch once; first at #25)** · ♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Hashing](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-4-hashing/) **(watch once; first at #1)**

**Return:** Maintain the current segment end and explain why cutting exactly when the scan reaches it is safe.

valid-parenthesis-string.title: Valid Parenthesis String
valid-parenthesis-string.markdown:
**Cue:** Compress all possible open-parenthesis balances into a feasible lower-to-upper range.

🔴 [Greedy Invariants — Concept Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W1hdYdsqBJo) · 🟡 [CodePath — Greedy Algorithms](https://guides.codepath.org/compsci/Greedy-Algorithms)

**Return:** Define both bounds, why the lower bound is clamped at zero, and when the upper bound proves failure.

insert-interval.title: Insert Interval
insert-interval.markdown:
**Cue:** A sorted interval list splits into intervals before, overlapping, and after the new interval.

🔴 [MIT 6.046 — Interval Scheduling](https://www.ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-046j-design-and-analysis-of-algorithms-spring-2015/resources/lecture-1-course-overview-interval-scheduling/) · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Sets and Sorting](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-3-sets-and-sorting/)

**Return:** State the three phases and why all overlapping intervals can be merged into one running interval.

merge-intervals.title: Merge Intervals
merge-intervals.markdown:
**Cue:** Sorting by start time makes every possible overlap appear next to the current merged interval.

♻️ [MIT 6.046 — Interval Scheduling](https://www.ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-046j-design-and-analysis-of-algorithms-spring-2015/resources/lecture-1-course-overview-interval-scheduling/) **(watch once; first at #130)** · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Sets and Sorting](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-3-sets-and-sorting/)

**Return:** Define the current merged interval and the exact overlap condition, including touching endpoints.

non-overlapping-intervals.title: Non-overlapping Intervals
non-overlapping-intervals.markdown:
**Cue:** When intervals conflict, keeping the one that finishes earlier preserves the most future space.

♻️ [MIT 6.046 — Interval Scheduling](https://www.ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-046j-design-and-analysis-of-algorithms-spring-2015/resources/lecture-1-course-overview-interval-scheduling/) **(watch once; first at #130)** · 🟡 [CodePath — Greedy Algorithms](https://guides.codepath.org/compsci/Greedy-Algorithms)

**Return:** Give the exchange argument for earliest finish and connect removals to the maximum compatible set.

meeting-rooms.title: Meeting Rooms
meeting-rooms.markdown:
**Cue:** After sorting by start time, only the previous meeting can conflict with the current one.

♻️ [MIT 6.046 — Interval Scheduling](https://www.ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-046j-design-and-analysis-of-algorithms-spring-2015/resources/lecture-1-course-overview-interval-scheduling/) **(watch once; first at #130)** · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Sets and Sorting](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-3-sets-and-sorting/)

**Return:** State the endpoint convention and explain why checking adjacent sorted intervals is sufficient.

meeting-rooms-ii.title: Meeting Rooms II
meeting-rooms-ii.markdown:
**Cue:** The answer is the maximum number of intervals active at the same time.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Binary Heaps](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-8-binary-heaps/) **(watch once; first at #5)** · 🟡 [MIT 6.046 — Interval Scheduling](https://www.ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-046j-design-and-analysis-of-algorithms-spring-2015/resources/lecture-1-course-overview-interval-scheduling/)

**Return:** Choose a min-heap of end times or a start/end sweep and state how equal timestamps are ordered.

minimum-interval-to-include-each-query.title: Minimum Interval to Include Each Query
minimum-interval-to-include-each-query.markdown:
**Cue:** Sort queries offline, add newly eligible intervals, and remove expired ones from a size-ordered heap.

🔴 [Offline Queries with a Sweep Line](https://cfstep.com/training/tutorials/general-techniques/answering-queries-offline-with-sweepline/) · 🟡 [MIT 6.006 — Binary Heaps](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-8-binary-heaps/)

**Return:** At query q, identify eligible, expired, heap key, and how answers return to original query order.

rotate-image.title: Rotate Image
rotate-image.markdown:
🚫 **No pre-watch.** Derive the coordinate mapping or the equivalent transpose-then-reverse transformation on a small square.

🟡 **After solve:** [Rotation Matrices and Coordinate Mapping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotation_matrix)

**Return:** Map `(row, column)` to its rotated coordinate and show every cell is moved exactly once.

spiral-matrix.title: Spiral Matrix
spiral-matrix.markdown:
🚫 **No pre-watch.** Maintain shrinking top, bottom, left, and right boundaries around the unvisited rectangle.

🟡 **After solve:** [Row-Major and Column-Major Order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Row-_and_column-major_order)

**Return:** State the remaining-region invariant and the checks needed before traversing the final row or column.

set-matrix-zeroes.title: Set Matrix Zeroes
set-matrix-zeroes.markdown:
🚫 **No pre-watch.** Reuse the first row and column as marker storage without losing their original zero state.

🟡 **After solve:** [Row-Major and Column-Major Order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Row-_and_column-major_order)

**Return:** Name the two extra flags and the safe order for marking, filling the interior, then filling borders.

happy-number.title: Happy Number
happy-number.markdown:
**Cue:** A deterministic number transformation either reaches one or eventually repeats a state.

♻️ [CP-Algorithms — Tortoise and Hare](https://cp-algorithms.com/others/tortoise_and_hare.html) **(watch once; first at #36)** · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Cycle Finding](https://visualgo.net/en/cyclefinding)

**Return:** Explain why repetition means a cycle and how slow and fast transformations detect it in constant space.

plus-one.title: Plus One
plus-one.markdown:
🚫 **No pre-watch.** Simulate carrying in positional notation from the least significant digit.

🟡 **After solve:** [Positional Notation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Positional_notation)

**Return:** Explain when the loop stops early and why an all-nine input needs one additional leading digit.

powx-n.title: Pow(x, n)
powx-n.markdown:
**Cue:** Read the exponent in binary and reuse successively squared powers.

🔴 [CP-Algorithms — Binary Exponentiation](https://cp-algorithms.com/algebra/binary-exp.html)

**Return:** Maintain `answer × base^remaining exponent = original power` and handle zero and negative exponents.

multiply-strings.title: Multiply Strings
multiply-strings.markdown:
🚫 **No pre-watch.** Rebuild grade-school multiplication with explicit digit positions and carry propagation.

🟡 **After solve:** [Multiplication Algorithms and Carry Propagation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiplication_algorithm) · [Positional Notation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Positional_notation)

**Return:** Explain contributions to positions `i+j` and `i+j+1`, carry normalization, and leading-zero removal.

detect-squares.title: Detect Squares
detect-squares.markdown:
**Cue:** Fix the query point, enumerate possible diagonal points, and retrieve the other corners by coordinates.

♻️ [MIT 6.006 — Hashing](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/resources/lecture-4-hashing/) **(watch once; first at #1)** · 🟡 [VisuAlgo — Hash Table](https://visualgo.net/en/hashtable)

**Return:** Derive both missing corners, reject zero side length, and multiply independent point frequencies.

single-number.title: Single Number
single-number.markdown:
**Cue:** Even-frequency values cancel under XOR.

🔴 [XOR — Intuition and Identities](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VPw9vPN-3ac) · 🟡 [Bit-Manipulation Toolkit](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1um-WUyjess)

**Return:** Use `x XOR x = 0`, `x XOR 0 = x`, associativity, and commutativity without memorizing a trick.

number-of-1-bits.title: Number of 1 Bits
number-of-1-bits.markdown:
**Cue:** Remove exactly one known set bit per iteration.

🔴 [CP-Algorithms — Bit Manipulation](https://cp-algorithms.com/algebra/bit-manipulation.html) · 🟡 [Bit-Manipulation Toolkit](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1um-WUyjess)

**Return:** Show algebraically why `n AND (n-1)` clears the lowest set bit and derive work proportional to set bits.

counting-bits.title: Counting Bits
counting-bits.markdown:
**Cue:** Each answer can reference a smaller integer obtained by dropping one known bit.

♻️ [CP-Algorithms — Bit Manipulation](https://cp-algorithms.com/algebra/bit-manipulation.html) **(watch once; first at #145)** · ♻️ [Dynamic Programming — Five-Step Framework](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aPQY__2H3tE) **(watch once; first at #99)**

**Return:** Derive either `bits[i] = bits[i >> 1] + (i AND 1)` or the lowest-set-bit recurrence.

reverse-bits.title: Reverse Bits
reverse-bits.markdown:

missing-number.title: Missing Number
missing-number.markdown:
**Cue:** Pair indices with values so every present number cancels and one unmatched value remains.

sum-of-two-integers.title: Sum of Two Integers
sum-of-two-integers.markdown:
**Cue:** Binary addition is carry-free XOR plus shifted carry bits.

🔴 [Two’s Complement — Concept Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lKTsv6iVxV4) · ♻️ [XOR — Intuition and Identities](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VPw9vPN-3ac) **(watch once; first at #144)** · 🟡 [Binary Integer Overflow](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WN8i5cwjkSE)

reverse-integer.title: Reverse Integer
reverse-integer.markdown:
**Cue:** Prevent fixed-width overflow before multiplying the partial result by ten and adding a digit.

♻️ [Two’s Complement — Concept Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lKTsv6iVxV4) **(watch once; first at #149)** · 🟡 [Binary Integer Overflow](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WN8i5cwjkSE)

**Return:** Derive the precondition for `result * 10 + digit`, including boundary digits for minimum and maximum integers.
